events.reason: Hemoptysis, weight loss, upper lobe infiltrates

documents.title: Hospital discharge summary
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital, inpatient medicine. Admitted 04/29/2022, discharged 05/06/2022. Copy to primary care on request.

Reason for admission: coughing up blood, unintended weight loss, upper lobe infiltrates on chest imaging.
History: 69-year-old man with a mechanical aortic valve on warfarin, atrial fibrillation, coronary disease with prior inferior MI, insulin-treated diabetes and hypertension. Weight 81 kg on admission, down from 87 kg at a February office visit.
Allergies: no known drug allergies.
Hospital course: placed in airborne isolation. Sputum acid-fast smear positive; nucleic acid amplification positive for M. tuberculosis complex. Diagnosis pulmonary tuberculosis, made 05/03. Four-drug therapy started 05/03: rifampin 600 mg, isoniazid 300 mg, pyrazinamide 2000 mg and ethambutol 1600 mg daily. Health department notified; care transferred to the regional TB clinic for directly observed therapy.
Anticoagulation: warfarin continued; rifampin is expected to lower its effect substantially. Anticoagulation clinic notified to increase INR checks.
Discharge medications: the TB regimen above; warfarin per anticoagulation clinic; metoprolol succinate 100 mg daily; lisinopril 20 mg daily; amlodipine 5 mg daily; metformin 1000 mg twice daily; insulin glargine 24 units nightly; atorvastatin 40 mg daily.
Follow-up: TB clinic, anticoagulation clinic, primary care.

documents.title: Patient reports hospitalization
documents.author: RN
documents.body:
Pt called to let us know he was admitted 4/29-5/6 at the regional hospital - coughing up blood, lost weight over the winter, and was told he has tuberculosis. Started on four TB pills on 5/3; the TB clinic watches him take them each day. Anticoag clinic aware. Feels tired but better, no blood in a week.
No discharge paperwork came to us. Request sent to the hospital. Offered a visit; he'd rather wait until he's out of isolation precautions per the TB clinic. Routed to PCP.

documents.title: PCP note on call
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Reviewed. TB clinic is running the regimen. Key issue for us is the rifampin-warfarin interaction with his mechanical valve - the anticoag clinic knows. Visit once cleared by the TB clinic.

conditions.note: blood-streaked sputum on warfarin during rifampin therapy

documents.title: Emergency department note
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital emergency department, visit 05/24/2022.

Chief concern: bleeding on warfarin.
HPI: 70-year-old man with a mechanical aortic valve on long-term warfarin and atrial fibrillation, discharged three weeks ago with newly diagnosed pulmonary tuberculosis, now on rifampin, isoniazid, pyrazinamide and ethambutol. Since last evening a small amount of blood streaking in his sputum. No other bleeding - no black stools, no nosebleeds, no bruising. No dietary change. His warfarin was increased last week after an INR of 1.2.
ROS: no chest pain, no shortness of breath, no melena.
Allergies: NKDA.
Vitals within normal limits. Exam: unremarkable; lungs without distress, mechanical valve click present.
INR today 1.7 - still below his goal.
Assessment: minor anticoagulation-related bleeding in a patient whose warfarin effect is being lowered by rifampin.
Plan: continue warfarin 10 mg daily; anticoagulation clinic to recheck INR in 3 days; TB clinic informed. Return for larger-volume blood, dizziness or black stools.

documents.title: Office visit - TB, warfarin, ED follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
First visit since his TB diagnosis. TB clinic cleared him to be seen; he's had four weeks of observed therapy. Hospital discharge summary still not received - working from his account, his pill bottles and the ED note (received 5/27).

Timeline per him and the ED note: admitted 4/29-5/6 with hemoptysis and weight loss, TB diagnosed 5/3, four drugs started. Anticoag clinic found INR 1.2 on 5/17 and raised warfarin to 10 mg. On 5/24 he had some blood-streaked sputum and went to the ED: INR 1.7, warfarin left at 10 mg, home.
Since then: no more blood. Cough much less. Appetite returning. No black stools, no bruising.

Exam: weight 82 kg (87 in Feb). Afebrile. Irregular rhythm, crisp click. Lungs: no distress, no crackles. No edema. No jaundice.

A/P
1. Pulmonary TB on RIPE - TB clinic directs. Added to list; drugs entered as outside-managed. CMP for liver tests today (TB clinic checks as well).
2. Anticoagulation-related bleeding (ED label), minor, resolved. Added to problem list.
3. Mechanical AVR/AF on warfarin with rifampin interaction - warfarin now 10 mg; dosing stays with anticoag clinic. Will update the list as they change it.
4. Diabetes - weight loss; watch for lows on glargine 24. No lows so far.
Visit again mid-August.

documents.title: Office visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Brought his bottles. Only rifampin and isoniazid now - the TB clinic stopped pyrazinamide and ethambutol on 7/5 at the end of the two-month phase; cultures negative by then and the organism is fully sensitive, per the clinic nurse. Nobody told us; our list had all four. Corrected today.
Discharge summary from the May admission still outstanding - third request sent.
Feels well. Weight coming back. No bleeding. INRs have been 'all over the place' but in range the last two checks on 10 mg, per him.
Exam: irregular, click, lungs clear, no edema.
A1c today, likely better with the weight loss. Continue. RTC December after he finishes TB treatment.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: A1c 7.1 - the lowest since you joined, likely the weight change this spring. No lows reported, so glargine stays at 24 units for now, but call if any morning sugar is under 80.

documents.title: Nurse visit - vaccines
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Flu high dose L deltoid, bivalent COVID R deltoid. Held pressure 2 minutes each, no oozing. He asked about the lung CT - PCP said to skip this year while the TB clinic is imaging him.

reports.text: Comparison: admission imaging April 2022. PA and lateral views. Upper lobe opacities have largely cleared, with residual linear scarring. No new consolidation. No effusion. No cavity. Sternotomy wires and prosthetic aortic valve. Heart size normal.
reports.conclusion: Improved upper lobe opacities with residual scarring, consistent with treated tuberculosis.

documents.title: TB clinic treatment completion letter
documents.author: infectious disease
documents.body:
Regional tuberculosis clinic - letter to primary care.
Re: William Howland, DOB 05/02/1952. Allergies: none known.

Mr. Howland has completed six months of directly observed therapy for drug-susceptible pulmonary tuberculosis. Intensive phase (rifampin, isoniazid, pyrazinamide, ethambutol) 05/03-07/05/2022; sputum cultures converted to negative within the first two months. Continuation phase with rifampin and isoniazid through 11/03/2022, when both were stopped. Liver tests stayed normal throughout.
End-of-treatment chest film 11/03: improved upper lobe opacities with residual scarring.
We have let his anticoagulation clinic know rifampin has stopped; warfarin needs will fall over the next several weeks.
No further TB clinic follow-up needed. Please call if new cough, hemoptysis or weight loss.

No falls. Independent. Recall 3/3. PHQ-2 0. Proxy on file.

reports.study: Low-dose CT chest for lung cancer screening
reports.text: Comparison: 10/28/2021. Low-dose non-contrast technique. Interval linear scarring in the upper lobes, consistent with history of treated tuberculosis. No pulmonary nodules. No consolidation, cavitation or effusion. Prosthetic aortic valve, sternotomy wires and coronary stent. No adenopathy.
reports.conclusion: Lung-RADS 2: benign-appearing upper lobe scarring from treated tuberculosis. No nodules. Annual screening.

documents.title: Hospital discharge summary - inferior STEMI
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Regional hospital, cardiology service. Admitted 11/15/2023 via the emergency department; discharged 11/18/2023. Sent to primary care on request.

Presentation: 71-year-old man with prior myocardial infarction, mechanical aortic valve on warfarin, atrial fibrillation, diabetes and hypertension, with pressure-like substernal chest pain spreading to the left arm, breathlessness and sweating.
ED: BP 160/90, HR 102, RR 22, SpO2 94% on room air. Regular rhythm; no murmur, rub or gallop; lungs clear. Troponin I 0.5 ng/mL (reference <0.04). Creatinine 1.2. A1c 7.8%. Total cholesterol 185. ECG: ST elevation in II, III and aVF.
Course: inferior STEMI. Emergent coronary angiography: culprit lesion in the mid right coronary artery, treated with one drug-eluting stent. Aspirin given during the hospital stay only. Warfarin continued. Uncomplicated recovery.
Allergies: no known drug allergies.
Discharge medications: clopidogrel 75 mg daily for 12 months (new); warfarin per anticoagulation clinic; metoprolol succinate 100 mg daily; lisinopril 20 mg daily; amlodipine 5 mg daily; atorvastatin 40 mg daily; metformin 1000 mg twice daily; insulin glargine 24 units nightly.
Follow-up: cardiology in 3 months; primary care within 2 weeks.

documents.title: Another heart attack
documents.author: patient
documents.body: I had another heart attack last Wednesday. Ambulance to the hospital, they put in a new stent and I came home Saturday. I'm on a new blood thinner pill along with the warfarin - clopidogrel. They said to see you in two weeks. Feeling sore but OK.

documents.title: RE: Another heart attack
documents.author: RN
documents.body: So sorry to hear it, and glad you're home. You're booked with the doctor Tuesday 11/28 at 10:20. Please bring every medicine you're taking and your hospital papers. Any chest pain at rest, black stools or bleeding that won't stop - call 911.

documents.title: Post-hospital visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen 10 days after discharge. No summary from the hospital yet; his account plus the bottles and the discharge med sheet he brought.
Woke 11/15 with chest pressure into the left arm, sweaty, short of breath. EMS, ED, cath lab - new stent in the right coronary, he was told. Home 11/18. Clopidogrel 75 daily added for a year alongside warfarin. Everything else unchanged.
Since: no chest pain. Walks the driveway twice a day. No bleeding, no black stools.
Exam: BP and HR as charted. Regular rhythm today, click crisp. Groin/wrist site clean. Lungs clear. No edema.
A/P
1. Inferior STEMI s/p RCA stent - added to list. Clopidogrel 75 for 12 months with warfarin. Cardiology follow-up booked for February.
2. Bleeding risk on two agents - reviewed warning signs. INR dosing still with the anticoag clinic.
3. Rest unchanged. Requested discharge summary and cath report.

documents.title: Clopidogrel refill request
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy request: clopidogrel 75 mg daily, original 30-day fill from the hospital. On list as of 11/28 for 12 months post stent. PCP approved 90 days with 2 refills. End date around mid-November 2024 noted on the order.
